title: Sita: Choosing the Forest
subtitle: A wife's argument against remaining in the palace

learningObjectives.text: What does Sita decide when Rama prepares to go to the forest?
Which source boundary is important when discussing this speech?

choice.author: Valmiki
choice.locator: Ayodhyakandam · Section XXVII; Ayodhyakandam · Section XXVII, normalized characters 955-1557
choice.excerpt: I shall go before thee, Oh Raghava, treading upon the thorns and prickly grass. Confident do thou take me with thee, Oh great hero, renouncing jealousy and indignation, like unto water left after drinking; there exists no sin in me that could justify forsaking. Unto woman is preferable under all circumtances the shade of her husband's feet to the tops of a palace, the celestial car or excursion in the airy path.[131] I have been taught by my father and mother to follow my husband in all conditions of life; and I shall carry out now what I have been taught; I shall not abide by any other counsel.
choice.note: Verbatim English translation from Dutt. The Mahabharata volume is a condensed verse rendering; the Ramayana volume contains only the Balakandam and Ayodhyakandam.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sita answers the exile
narrativeBlocks.body: When Rama prepares to leave for the forest, Sita argues that she will go with him rather than remain in the palace.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sita states her choice
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Dutt's English rendering; whitespace normalized): “I shall go before thee, Oh Raghava, treading upon the thorns and prickly grass. Confident do thou take me with thee, Oh great hero, renouncing jealousy and indignation, like unto water left after drinking; there exists no sin in me that could justify forsaking. Unto woman is preferable under all circumtances the shade of her husband's feet to the tops of a palace, the celestial car or excursion in the airy path.[131] I have been taught by my father and mother to follow my husband in all conditions of life; and I shall carry out now what I have been taught; I shall not abide by any other counsel.”

narrativeBlocks.title: A reasoned appeal
narrativeBlocks.body: Sita invokes the teaching she says she received from her parents and insists that she will follow Rama. The lesson stays with Dutt's translated speech rather than treating it as a rule for all women.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read the text's own voice carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: This passage is Dutt's English prose translation of one Ayodhyakandam section. Its gendered language belongs to this scene and translation; it should not be made into a universal statement about Indian women or practice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Sita is an active speaker
narrativeBlocks.body: In this episode, Sita argues for her own course and gives reasons rather than remaining a silent object in Rama's decision.
